exercise.name: Weighted Full Squat from Deficit

reference.title: Weighted Full Squat from Deficit
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

equipment: Dip belt with a weight plate

breathing.pattern: Big breath in and brace at the top, hold it on the way down and through the bottom, breathe out as you pass the hardest part of the rise or at the top.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, a short pause, about 1.2 s up

prescription.tempo: 2-0-1-0 (2 s down, no pause, 1 s up)
prescription.load: Plate load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can squat to full depth with the form shown, leaving about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Add 2.5-5 kg when every rep of every set reaches full depth with good form.

cues.text: Stand with one foot on each box, feet a little wider than the hips, toes turned out; the dip belt sits low on the hips and the plate hangs on its chain between the boxes. Arms reach forward for balance.
Big breath, brace, then sit straight down between the heels: knees travel forward and out over the toes, chest stays up, the plate drops between the boxes.
Hips below the knees, heels flat on the boxes, back flat; the plate stays clear of the floor.
Drive the boxes away, hips and chest rising together; knees keep pushing out. Breathe out as you pass the hardest part.
Stand tall, take a new breath and brace; keep the plate from swinging.

mistakes.mistake: Plate hitting the floor at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Use taller boxes or a shorter chain.

mistakes.mistake: Knees caving in on the way up
mistakes.fix: Push the knees out over the toes; use a lighter plate.
Keep the whole foot down; work on ankle mobility or sit a little less deep.
Move smoothly and pause briefly at the top.

kinematics.setup: 44 cm between the ankle centres (≈1.1x the rig's 40 cm shoulder width), toes out 28°
kinematics.norm: About hip to shoulder width with the toes out about 20-30 degrees (Lorenzetti 2018; Sinclair 2022); wider stances moved demand toward the hip (Paoli 2009)

kinematics.peak: ≈122°; hip joints 4.1 cm below the knee joints
kinematics.norm: A full squat takes the hip crease below the top of the knee, about 115-130 degrees of knee flexion (clinical opinion; Straub 2024)
Large hip flexion at full depth; the trunk lean adds to it (Straub 2024)
High-bar squats keep the trunk more upright than low-bar squats; a front squat is more upright still (Glassbrook-style comparisons summarised in Larsen 2021; Gullett 2009)

kinematics.peak: 2.0 s down, 0.4 s pause, 1.2 s up, 1.6 s reset
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Feet on two 20 cm boxes; plate (30 cm) 39 cm below the hip joints
kinematics.peak: Plate 6.9 cm above the floor at the bottom, between the boxes (11.8 cm to spare each side)
kinematics.norm: The load hangs from the hips, so the spine and shoulders carry none of it; the boxes let the plate travel below the feet (common coaching)

sources.title: GymVisual, Weighted Full Squat from Deficit, video (movement reference)

Larsen et al. 2021, stance width and bar placement in back squats: kinematics, kinetics and EMG (Front Sports Act Living)
Gullett, Tillman, Gutierrez & Chow 2009, a biomechanical comparison of back and front squats in healthy trained individuals (J Strength Cond Res 23(1):284-292; PubMed 19002072)
Paoli, Marcolin and Petrone 2009, effect of stance width on EMG of eight thigh muscles during the back squat (J Strength Cond Res)

Contreras, Vigotsky, Schoenfeld, Beardsley & Cronin 2015, a comparison of gluteus maximus, biceps femoris and vastus lateralis EMG in the back squat and barbell hip thrust (J Appl Biomech 31(6):452-458)

cautions: Use two stable boxes of the same height, wide enough for the whole foot, set where they cannot slide.
Fit the dip belt low on the hips and check the chain before loading it.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee or hip pain: squat to a pain-free depth.
Low boxes: shorten the chain so the plate clears the floor.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Knee extensors control the descent and drive the rise; they work hardest near the bottom (Straub 2024). Back squat vastus lateralis activity was higher than in the hip thrust (Contreras 2015).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Knee extensors control the descent and drive the rise; they work hardest near the bottom (Straub 2024). Back squat vastus lateralis activity was higher than in the hip thrust (Contreras 2015).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Main hip extensor, working hardest out of the bottom of a full squat (clinical opinion; Straub 2024).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Main hip extensor, working hardest out of the bottom of a full squat (clinical opinion; Straub 2024).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus helps extend the hip from deep flexion; wider stances raised adductor activity (Paoli 2009).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus helps extend the hip from deep flexion; wider stances raised adductor activity (Paoli 2009).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension; their length changes little in a squat, so activity stays moderate (Contreras 2015).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension; their length changes little in a squat, so activity stays moderate (Contreras 2015).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the back flat against the forward lean the bar on the shoulders creates.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the back flat against the forward lean the bar on the shoulders creates.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Control the forward travel of the knees over the planted feet.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Control the forward travel of the knees over the planted feet.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing (breath held against a tight midsection) stiffens the trunk under the bar.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Part of the brace around the trunk.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Part of the brace around the trunk.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the knee tracking over the foot and the pelvis level.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the knee tracking over the foot and the pelvis level.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Hold the arms forward for balance.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Hold the arms forward for balance.
